Technology stocks were losing ground in recent trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing more than 0.6% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was dropping nearly 0.4%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Xunlei ( XNET ) was hanging on to a 1% increase Monday afternoon, easing from a more than 5% advance earlier Monday for the cloud-based technology company that followed it announcing a new strategic partnership with Newland Hi-Tech Group to research and develop new products and services. As part of of the new partnership, Xunlei signed a series of transactions with a Newland-affiliated company, Beijing LinkChain Co Ltd, to transfer exclusive rights to operate the LinkToken program within mainland China.
In other sector news:
(+) Quantum Corp. ( QTM ) soared on Friday, topping out with a more than 24% increase, after the data-storage company late Friday a special board committee has completed its internal investigation into its financial statements, saying it will restate financial results for its fiscal years ended March 31, 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2018, because some revenue was recognized prematurely under GAAP procedures. The company said between $25 million to $35 million in revenue was improperly recognized prior to Sept. 30, 2017, with another $15 million to $25 million of premature revenue on the books through June 30, 2018.
(-) Sensata Technologies Holding plc ( ST ) declined as much as 8% on Monday after analysts at Morgan Stanley cut their stock rating for the electronic sensors and controls manufacturer to Underweight from Equal Weight previously and also lowered their price target for the company's stock by $8 a share.
